question: Should this branch remain the canonical ACP node-backed runtime implementation path, or should maintainers pause it and require narrower storage/protocol/security slices first?
rationale: The branch is a broad new runtime and gateway-node command surface with concrete correctness blockers and a storage-policy conflict, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term product and security boundary on behalf of maintainers.

options.title: Require rework before merge
options.body: Keep the branch open but require SQLite storage, event-failure propagation, projection/reconnect/run-id fixes, real behavior proof, and security review before another merge attempt.

options.title: Split into staged PRs
options.body: Pause or supersede this branch with smaller storage, protocol, node-host, and replay slices that can each get focused proof and owner review.

options.title: Accept the broad runtime risk
options.body: Maintainership can intentionally accept the new runtime surface after proof, but that would own the JSON state, delivery, reconnect, and security-boundary risks called out here.

recommendation.title: Require rework before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the branch open but require SQLite storage, event-failure propagation, projection/reconnect/run-id fixes, real behavior proof, and security review before another merge attempt.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history shows broad ACP dispatch, gateway, docs, and node command ownership signals for the affected decision surface.
